questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question_text: A 2-month-old male infant is brought to the clinic for a routine check-up. The mother notes that the child has been increasingly irritable and exhibits a peculiar, musty odor in his urine. Physical examination reveals a noticeably fair complexion, light blonde hair, and early developmental delay. A deficiency in which of the following enzymes is responsible for this condition?
questions.explanation: PKU: phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency → phenylalanine accumulates → phenylpyruvate in urine (musty odor), intellectual disability, fair complexion. Diet: restrict phenylalanine.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question_text: A 34-year-old male presents with persistent fatigue, bone pain, and abdominal fullness. Physical examination reveals massive splenomegaly and moderate hepatomegaly. Bone marrow aspirate is performed, showing large, lipid-laden macrophages with a distinctive cytological appearance resembling 'wrinkled tissue paper'. Which of the following enzymes is deficient in this patient?
questions.explanation: Gaucher disease: most common lysosomal storage disease. Glucocerebrosidase deficiency → glucocerebroside accumulation. Gaucher cells (wrinkled tissue paper appearance) in liver/spleen/bone marrow.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question_text: A 24-year-old military recruit traveling abroad is prescribed primaquine for malaria prophylaxis. A few days later, he presents to an emergency department with severe fatigue, dark, tea-colored urine, and yellowish discoloration of his sclera. Lab work demonstrates an acute episode of hemolytic anemia. This clinical presentation is fundamentally caused by a functional deficiency in an enzyme that serves which cellular role?

options.A: First committed step of glycolysis to generate ATP
options.B: Rate-limiting step of the pentose phosphate pathway to maintain reduced glutathione
options.C: Final step of anaerobic glycolysis in red blood cells

questions.explanation: G6PD deficiency: X-linked. G6PD generates NADPH via pentose phosphate pathway → maintains GSH → protects RBCs from oxidative stress. Trigger: infections, drugs (primaquine, dapsone).

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question_text: A biochemistry student is studying cell culture metabolic dynamics under conditions of high intracellular ATP and citrate concentrations. She observes a profound slowing down of glucose utilization through the glycolytic pathway. Which of the following rate-limiting enzymes of glycolysis is directly inhibited by these high-energy state indicators?
questions.explanation: PFK-1 is the key regulatory enzyme of glycolysis. Inhibited by: ATP, citrate. Activated by: AMP, ADP, fructose-2,6-bisphosphate (most potent activator). Site of glycolytic control.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question_text: A 14-month-old boy is brought to the pediatric clinic due to severe developmental delays, spasticity, and a striking tendency to bite his own lips and fingers, causing noticeable ulcerations. The parents also report finding orange, sand-like crystals in his diapers. This severe neurodevelopmental disorder is caused by a failure of the purine salvage pathway due to a total deficiency of which enzyme?
questions.explanation: This case describes Lesch-Nyhan syndrome, an X-linked recessive disorder characterized by intellectual disability, severe self-mutilation, and hyperuricemia (orange crystals in diaper). It is caused by a structural or functional absence of HGPRT, which converts hypoxanthine to IMP and guanine to GMP in the purine salvage pathway, causing excess purine synthesis and uric acid overproduction.
